objectClass.notes: Three admitted views describe one clean stylized fantasy inn. The front fixes the gable width, sign placement, entrance, and bay-window proportions; the side fixes building depth, tile-course count, chimney location, two upper windows, one lower window, and the timber network. The hidden rear repeats the observed construction conservatively. This is a procedural stylized reconstruction, not survey geometry or photoreal inverse rendering.

reasoning: The macro silhouette combines a two-storey wall volume, one closed gable-roof prism, a chimney, a projecting faceted bay, a hanging sign, and entrance props.
Half-timber construction requires separate plaster shells, floor belt, corner posts, front gable posts, side rails, straight diagonals, and curved braces on both visible elevations.
Identity depends on regular repeated systems: clay roof tiles, ridge caps, chimney blocks, windows, shutters, muntins, diamond lattice, chain links, door planks, barrel staves, leaves, and flowers.
The sign, door, shutters, flower box, barrel, and bay window require explicit parent sockets or contact contracts so they do not float.
The clean stylized palette contains many distinct material families while deliberately avoiding photoreal micro-noise.
Three mutually distinct views reduce geometric uncertainty; only the rear elevation remains inferred.

specDepthDecision.rationale: A shallow box facade would lose the closed roof volume, dense timber skeleton, projecting bay, regular tile and lattice systems, and the attached sign/door/flower/barrel props.

detailInventory.note: Twenty-two consolidated identity systems come from the three filled view inventories. Every item maps to a component localFeature or material localOverride that the sculpt spec must contain.

details.description: One closed triangular prism supplies both roof slopes, eaves, underside, and front/rear gable caps.
Regular overlapping red clay tile rows step down both roof slopes with staggered vertical joints.
A regular cap row follows the full ridge and is thicker than the field tiles.
Rounded grey blocks form staggered chimney courses with recessed joints, a shoulder block, and projecting cap.
The front gable uses a center post, collar beam, and mirrored inward-curving braces raised above plaster.
Posts, rails, straight lower diagonals, and tall curved braces articulate both storeys on the visible side.
Upper and side windows use four amber panes, thick muntins, raised timber heads and sills, and paired ivory shutters.
A three-face projecting ground-floor bay uses thick chamfered timber corner posts, header, sill, and side returns.
Black raised diamond leading repeats across the front and angled side panes of the bay.
All glazing is warm amber; the projecting bay is the strongest light source and needs restrained emissive intensity.
The timber door has recessed vertical plank seams, two black strap hinges, and a raised pull under a thick lintel.
A black wall plate and horizontal bracket carry two articulated chain drops with visible air gaps.
The hanging burgundy sign has a stepped scalloped edge, thin gold inset border, and raised black foaming-mug emblem.
A projecting timber planter supports layered foliage, red blossom clusters, and hanging vines below the bay sill.
details.scale: meso planter with micro botanical repeat

details.description: A bulged barrel uses alternating vertical staves, three dark hoops, and a recessed top rim.
Timber edges use clean chamfers and restrained lengthwise value bands rather than noisy photoreal grain.
details.scale: micro edge and meso color treatment

details.description: Warm ivory plaster has low-frequency bay-to-bay value variation and slightly darker timber contact zones.
Chimney mortar gaps are darker than stone faces without random surface speckle.
Tile rows alternate across a restrained brick-red palette; joints read through geometry, not noisy albedo.
The matte burgundy sign face is separated from a slightly smoother gold border and black raised emblem.
Ivory shutters use shallow recessed inner panels and chamfered outer frames.
A continuous deep timber belt separates storeys and is supported by short downward block brackets.

anatomy.note: Not a character or hybrid subject.

definitionOfDone: The model reads immediately as the same compact two-storey half-timber fantasy inn from front, side, and three-quarter views.
The building uses one closed solid gable-roof prism with regular geometric tile relief; paired rotated box slabs are prohibited.
Warm plaster, raised timber frame, red tile roof, stone chimney, hanging burgundy mug sign, glowing faceted bay, timber door, barrel, and flower box remain separately readable.
The factory returns an action-ready THREE.Group with facade +Z, visible sole y=0, and named hinges, sign pivot, sockets, colliders, and destruction groups.
Visible materials are MeshStandardMaterial or MeshToonMaterial-compatible color blocks with clean bevels, restrained scalar variation, and no facade photo or texture billboard.

featureGroups.name: Closed red-tile gable roof and compact inn massing
qualityCriteria: One manifold prism supplies both roof slopes, underside, eaves, and gable caps.
Wall width/depth, floor split, eave height, ridge height, and chimney placement agree across all three views.
Regular relief tiles and ridge caps sit on the solid roof rather than becoming structural slabs.

featureGroups.name: Half-timber plaster shell and shuttered windows
qualityCriteria: Raised posts, rails, belt beam, straight diagonals, and curved braces remain separate depth layers over plaster.
The front gable and long side use the distinct bracing rhythms established by their references.
Window heads, sills, muntins, warm panes, and paired panelled shutters remain legible.

featureGroups.name: Projecting faceted bay with warm diamond-lattice glazing
qualityCriteria: A real three-face bay projects beyond the ground-floor facade with corner posts, header, sill, front pane, and angled returns.
Raised black diamond leading remains regular on every visible pane.
Amber glazing is emissive enough to read warm without erasing lattice contrast.

featureGroups.name: Hanging mug sign, timber door, barrel, and flower box
qualityCriteria: The sign hangs from a projecting iron bracket through two chain runs and uses a scalloped burgundy plate, gold border, and raised black mug.
The timber door includes a hinge pivot, plank grooves, strap hinges, and pull.
The barrel uses staves and hoops; the planter uses a solid box plus repeated foliage, red blossoms, and trailing vines.
failureModes: single green box standing in for flowers

featureGroups.name: Clean bright stylized material separation
qualityCriteria: Plaster, stained timber, red tile, grey stone, burgundy paint, gold trim, black iron, ivory shutters, warm glass, foliage, and flowers remain distinct under neutral light.
Chamfers, real seams, module spacing, and clean low-frequency value bands carry form detail; photoreal micro-noise is absent.
Neutral, grazing, and reference-matched review views preserve material readability.

antiShallowSpecRules: Reject paired rotated box roof slabs, open roofs, and facade-only roof planes.
Reject wall textures or painted lines standing in for the raised half-timber network.
Reject facade photo planes, projected reference photos, sprites, and billboard substitutes.
Reject unmapped inventory details and generic feature-review targets.
Reject sign, shutters, door, flower box, barrel, chimney, or lattice without complete attachment/contact data.
Reject material families without independent albedo, roughness, tactile relief intent, frequency bands, and local overrides.

Reference PBR crop extraction is intentionally omitted because the accepted target is a clean stylized flat-color prop and the user prohibits photoreal micro-noise; solid albedo, geometric relief, and independent scalar PBR channels are the correct implementation.
qualityContract.referencePbrLimitation: The reference images intentionally depict clean stylized material blocks rather than patterned or photoreal finishes. Reference-derived texture crops would import baked lighting and unwanted micro-noise. Important relief is therefore geometric, colors are solid sampled families, and albedo/roughness/normal/AO intent remains independent through scalar and procedural descriptions.

authoringInstruction: Assessment completed from direct inspection of three admitted references and three filled detail inventories.
